title: The inflated figure
subtitle: Down 39% from peak — while the quoted figure barely moves
source: RTR-WP-001, The Critical CapEx India Won't Commit: Public Libraries in the Capital-Expenditure Decade, 2014-15 to 2024-25 (v3.1.2).
caption: India's per-capita public-library expenditure, 2018-19 (the series peak) to 2024-25. The nominal figure — state MH 2205-105 spending divided by the fixed Census 2011 population, the number usually quoted — barely falls. Once RRRLF Central transfers are added, the total is deflated to constant 2011-12 rupees, and the Technical Group's actual annual population projections replace the fixed 2011 Census count, the real, consolidated figure tells a sharper story: a collapse to ₹4.15 by 2021-22, recovering only to ₹5.00 — still 39% below its own peak. Adding capital spending on library buildings (₹1.10) gives ₹6.10, the campaign's headline number.

data.label: Nominal (as published)
data.note: State MH 2205-105 spending ÷ the fixed Census 2011 population — the figure usually quoted. Looks almost stable.

data.label: Real (consolidated)
